answer: Every session carries a proof-of-work stamp computed over the session identifier and the current epoch; the stamp is cheap for one real user but expensive at farm scale. The network verifies the stamp before accepting any state-changing action, so opening a thousand fake sessions costs a thousand stamps. The record keeps every ripple visible, so anyone can audit the session history. A hollow and a atlas may look alike, but only the session with a consistent pattern is honoured.
